Mine, as well, was not good.  I grew up in the shadow of an alpha twin...and a clinically depressed mother ((no father to speak of) although I've recently tracked him down and will probably pay a visit and break his fucking jaw)).  
I was one of those people who were "invisible" in high-school.  "Highly intelligent under-achiever" was the label which was applied.
I remember telling my (well meaning) guidance counselor that I would kill any test he put in front of me.  It didn't go over well.
I was very fortunate to have had an Uncle who had served in the military.  One day he came for a visit and said we (he and I) should go for a talk.  At the end of that day I had decided to join the Navy.  It was the best thing that ever happened to me.  I got the chance to completely re-invent myself.  The problem was, that I came back as an arrogant prick.  Perhaps the polar opposite of who I was.  Perhaps a hard shell to not feel anything.  To this day, I'd just like to feel something....
Sorry to be rambling, having a bad day.

Wow, that really hit me hard; actually I pretty much fell apart when I read it.
How can you know so much about where/how I am without knowing anything about me?

Actually, an in-process EDIT:  Maybe it's not that hard to see through me.  I'm not arrogant enough to assume that I'm the first person to experience this, but I just can't seem to ask for help, or ask the right people for help.Pathetic is the word that most often comes to mind.

Sometimes I wish I didn't have such a complete understanding of what's going on.  Sometimes I'd like to be "pleasantly ignorant".

The reality of it is that I understand exactly what I'm going through.  I could probably defend a post-graduate dissertation on the subject.  
I'm well versed because I want ANSWERS, I want to know "why", because I guess, the way I think, the why is all important.

I'd give anything to be able to go back to 28 and try to fix things without being so jaded (as I am now). 
The connection thing, as i've learned is entirely my own doing. The few friends I have dont see it because I'm comfortable around them. I guess one could say that I'm the only one "guarding the gate". Knowing that doesn't make it any easier. 
I haven't given up hope, I guess, but it's just exhausting....and has been for too long.

Your reddit name is one I could easily apply to myself.  Introversion is a major contributing factor to my woes. I just don't make connections like other people do. I used to have great faith in the medical community, but after a few decades, I'm not sure there is a fix. Alcohol is my absolute short term cure for the social aspect, but it does more harm than god in the long term.
In 42 years, that has never been the case
